Assess a fitted ecological taxonomy

Source: R/assessment.R
assess_taxonomy.Rd

Tests strict mean-step ordering and travelling concentration greater than foraging (or encamped). For HDT, the unadjusted 95 percent Wald interval of the target coefficient must be entirely positive. A significantly negative target coefficient does not establish attraction. Numerical failure and failed ecological rules remain distinct in the returned checks.

Usage

assess_taxonomy(
  fit,
  taxonomy,
  convention,
  target = "cos_diff_theta_to_target",
  min_occupancy = 0.05,
  persistence_bounds = c(0.05, 0.95),
  min_mean_gap = 0,
  score_tolerance = 0.01
)

Arguments

fit

An ssf_fit object.

taxonomy

One of HDT_F_R, T_F_R, T_E, or Other, or a specification created with ssf_taxonomy().

convention

Kernel convention passed to movement_metrics().

target

Name of a target-direction coefficient for HDT.

min_occupancy

Minimum Viterbi occupancy, between zero and one.

persistence_bounds

Open lower and upper self-transition bounds. For daily transitions, the bounds apply at each of the 24 hours.

min_mean_gap

Nonnegative minimum absolute gap between ordered means, in step-length units. This is not a significance test.

score_tolerance

Maximum absolute objective gradient for accepting a numerically stationary fit. Missing or nonfinite scores fail this check.

Value

A list with accepted, named logical checks, state labels, metrics, occupancy, and reasons. Wald intervals do not adjust for model selection and numerical convergence alone does not establish adequacy.
